title: Low-fidelity Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus polymerase mutants to improve live-attenuated vaccine safety and efficacy.
ehr_evidence: This study utilized in vitro cell cultures (Vero, HEK-293, BHK, C7/10, U4.4) and in vivo murine models (6-day-old and 7-week-old CD-1 mice) for viral passaging, plaque assays, and survival/immunogenicity testing.
summary: Experimental study evaluating low-fidelity RdRp mutations in the Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV) TC-83 vaccine strain to assess attenuation, immunogenicity, and genetic stability in cell culture and murine models.
key_findings: TC-83 3x and 4x mutants produced significantly higher mean neutralizing antibody titers compared with TC-83 (p = 0.0049 and p = 0.0012, respectively; n = 8 per group).
All vaccinated animals (n = 8 per group) showed complete protection from weight loss and death following lethal VEEV challenge, whereas sham-vaccinated controls all succumbed by Day 9.
TC-83 3x was significantly more virulent than parent virus in intracranial infant mice (mean time to death 3.91 days vs 5.36–5.54 days, p < 0.05).
Subcutaneous injection of 3x and 4x mutants in infant mice initially showed reduced mortality compared to TC-83, but outcomes varied significantly by electroporation pool.
After 10 serial intracranial passages in infant mice, 3x and 4x mutants reached virulence equivalent to unpassaged TC-83 and could not increase virulence past that point.
TC-83 4x passage 10 survived up to 1 week longer than passage 5, suggesting decreased fitness with additional passaging.
Illumina sequencing showed the 3x mutant produced a significantly higher amount of genetic diversity than parental TC-83, independent of the cell type used.
captured_features: genetic diversity and mutation frequency via Illumina sequencing
study_design: Experimental in vitro and in vivo murine model study
data_source_type: Cell culture and animal model data
population: Vero, HEK-293, BHK, C7/10, U4.4 cell lines; 6-day-old and 7-week-old CD-1 mice
exposure_domain: Viral RdRp fidelity mutations and nucleoside analog treatment
limitations: Phenotypic instability of low-fidelity mutants dependent on electroporation pool and mutant spectrum
Lack of atomic resolution structure for alphavirus RdRp limits mechanistic understanding
Results derived exclusively from murine models and cell culture, lacking human clinical or epidemiological data
Short-term passaging may not reflect long-term vaccine stability in natural settings
data_availability_statement: Data are not publically available, but will be provided upon request.
